To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) human social instincts can be identified that influence human behavior within corporations, (2) these social instincts are a result of the coevolution of human cognitive dispositions and cultural environments, and (3) the development of corporate cultures can be explained by a coevolutionary model of human social instincts.

the coevolution between the human mind and culture has led to the emergence of a variety of human social instincts that influence human behavior and the development of corporate cultures in an organizational context, while the nature of corporate cultures can be described as the result of the interaction between the social instincts of the employees and the corporate culture that has evolved in an organizational context and is embedded in the wider cultural context.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the social instincts of humans influence their behavior within corporations, how they are developed, and how they interact with other cognitive dispositions of the human brain.

the question of how corporate cultures emerge and develop over time and how the interaction between human social instincts and corporate cultures influences the nature of economic behavior and corporate performance.
the role of instincts and their interaction with the cultural environment in the development of corporate cultures.

the instinct theory of Veblen and his followers was not only wrong in its basic assumptions and in its predictions, but that the whole theory of instincts is not even a scientific one.
the role of instincts is to be considered as a neglected aspect in institutionalist theory.

the role of instincts for the development of corporate cultures has been neglected by institutionalists and that a more comprehensive analysis of the role of human social instincts is necessary to understand the dynamics of corporate cultures and the nature of the modern corporation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social instincts identified in this paper are a result of human coevolution with other humans.
we have shown how a theory of corporate cultures can be developed that takes the role of instincts into account and which deviates from orthodox economic theory.
the role of instincts is not limited to a biological or psychological level of analysis but can be used to explain social behavior in general and corporate cultures in particular.
The main takeaway from our work is that

instincts play an important role in the development and functioning of corporate cultures, and that a more detailed analysis of the role of social instincts can contribute new aspects in debates on the nature and functioning of corporations.
